Thanks Camila. Quick legal notes after a first pass on Nimbus's file:
1) Terminology: replace generic "cap"/"floor" with defined terms in Exhibit C (e.g., "Monthly Spend Ceiling", "Monthly Commit Floor"). This avoids ambiguity about cadence.
2) SKU migration: add language that operations will prorate a SKU across the bands based on actual days in band within the billing period. E.g., if a SKU spends 10 days in Band A and 20 days in Band B, charges prorated accordingly.
3) Soft cap / onboarding buffer: acceptable as a commercial concession if limited to the first two billing periods and capped at a fixed USD amount per month (suggest $25k/month buffer for first two months). Require written confirmation from Nimbus to enable buffer.
4) Audit and true-up: include a quarterly reconciliation clause with a 60-day dispute window. Keep the true-up asymmetric (we preserve the right to invoice underage but limit overnight capacity reallocation without 10-day notice).

I'll draft a redline that preserves Redwood's right to manage Dedicated capacity (so we can deny persistent overage cases) while giving Nimbus a predictable ramp. Marissa — I need the commercial tradeoff (credits budget) so legal can tie a dollar figure into the draft.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Agree with Karthik's framing. Commercially, here's an option that has been acceptable to similar customers: offer a banded "onboarding credit" that phases down. Example (illustrative):
- Months 1-2: 100% credit on incremental usage above commit up to $25k/month (buffer)
- Months 3-4: 50% credit on incremental usage above commit up to $15k/month
- Month 5+: no onboarding credit (normal true-up applies)

Example calculation: Commit = $200k/month. Actual M1 usage = $230k -> Over = $30k. We credit $25k (100%), customer pays $5k + applicable overage pricing.

If we go with prorated band migration, that reduces the need for a large buffer. My commercial recommendation: offer the two-month $25k buffer (as Karthik suggested) and attach a one-time onboarding credit of $10k in the order form to sweeten fast-sign. That keeps our downside bounded.

Laura — will this change how we reason about Dedicated pool sizing (i.e., do we carry extra headroom for the onboarding period)? If yes, we should record expected headroom in the order form.

– Marissa
Senior Sales Lead, Redwood Inference

Sanjay — thanks for the detailed redline. After internal review we propose the following compromise and attached redline (ExhibitC_Redline_v3_for_signature.pdf):

1) Definitions: "Monthly Commit Floor" and "Monthly Spend Ceiling" added to Exhibit C with clear monthly cadence.
2) SKU migration: charges will be prorated by days-in-band within the billing period (example clause added and a sample calculation included).
3) Onboarding buffer: two-month soft cap limited to $25,000 per month (applies only if Nimbus confirms onboarding start date in writing). Months 1-2 are eligible for the buffer, Month 3 reverts to standard true-up.
4) Credits: Redwood will apply a one-time onboarding credit of $10,000 on the first invoice following go-live.
5) Reconciliation: quarterly true-up with a 60-day dispute window. Redwood reserves capacity-management rights for persistent overages with 10-day notice.
